Lent a hand by Lloyd Webber’s sumptuous tunes, so too does this Phantom.

Forget panto, Into the Woods is theatre’s classiest Christmas show … This beautiful production of Stephen Sondheim’s fairytale musical is good enough to outlive the festive season … ... Jordan Fein, whose beautiful production for the Bridge Theatre makes a classy alternative to panto yet is richly detailed enough long to outlive the festive season.

“It’s not the most obvious choice of material for a venue as hip as the Donmar Warehouse”, but it makes “an evening of genial entertainment”, writes Clive Davis , while Andrzej Lukowski labels it a “somewhat dated, but thoroughly delightful social comedy” that “stands out from the period pack by sheer weight of northern-ness”.
The stakes are never too high, the tantrums never too long. As the night draws to a close, the couples are a little shaken, and all the better for it.
This musical has an unmistakably elegant froideur about it, making it easier to admire than love.
For Dave Fargnoli , it is a "sweet-natured comedy" that "gently probes tensions between social classes".

“Cook brings precise, physical comedy to the small role of the photographer from the Yorkshire Argus” who “gets slowly drunker as the mayhem unfolds around him,” notes Sarah Crompton , while Claire Allfree hails his “masterful miniature portrait of hapless humanity”.
